title: Eko straža “Protest for harmless air” in Belgrade
location: Belgrade: Slavija Square, with a march along Nemanjina to the Government of Serbia
scope: Belgrade gathering and march. Organizers framed demands as applying nationally; the reviewed sources do not establish simultaneous completed gatherings in other cities on 10 January.
participants_original: Balkan Green Energy News: “several thousand”; 2,000–3,000 in the procession. Nova.rs: security estimated about 1,000, while some participants and organizers claimed several thousand.
threshold_50_evidence: The lowest described estimate is approximately 1,000 (Nova.rs); another contemporary report estimates 2,000–3,000 in the procession. These approximate, conflicting reports both place attendance well above 50.

title.summary: Contemporary reporting identifies Eko straža’s clean-air protest in Belgrade.

start_date.summary: RFE/RL and two contemporaneous reports date the gathering to 10 January 2021.

end_date.summary: Nova.rs says organizers ended the protest by attaching demands to the Government building door, but does not report that participants departed or dissolved. Physical end date remains unknown under the unit rule.

location.summary: The gathering began at Slavija Square and the column walked to the Government building along Nemanjina Street.

scope.summary: A Belgrade protest is established. National framing of demands does not establish additional concurrent city gatherings.

organizer.summary: The reports name Eko straža as organizer.

demands.summary: Organizers demanded clean-air and environmental protections, public information and policy action from Serbian institutions. The broad political_behavior_process category is used for domestic policy choices; no land-use claim is coded.

participants_original.summary: Nova.rs records an approximate security estimate and a higher organizer/participant estimate; Balkan Green Energy News reports several thousand and a 2,000–3,000 range for the procession.

participants_min.summary: No exact numerical lower bound is assigned because the reported values are approximate and conflict.

participants_max.summary: No exact upper bound is established; the largest reported amount is qualitative (“several thousand”).

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Both published attendance accounts are far above 50 even at the lower reported estimate.

protester_violence.summary: The reviewed report does not describe protester violence; silence is retained as unknown.

state_response.accommodation.summary: Reports say demands were left at the Government building; Nova.rs says organizers planned formal delivery the next day. A September organizer later said little had changed, but no reviewed source establishes a January meeting, reception or explicit state refusal. Unknown.

state_response.arrests.summary: No event-specific arrest account appears in the reviewed passages; unknown.

state_response.beatings.summary: No event-specific beating account appears in the reviewed passages; unknown.

state_response.crowd_dispersal.summary: No dispersal attempt is described. The article notes no visible police/security, which does not prove there was no state action; unknown.

state_response.ignore.summary: In a 19 February organizer open letter, Eko straža says the prime minister had not answered the demands after 30 days from submission; the only reaction it identifies was the President’s public remarks, which did not address the demands. This is first-party evidence of nonresponse to the demands after the 10 January event, not an inference from silence in event coverage. The exact submission date and an official receipt/response are uncorroborated.

state_response.killings.summary: No event-specific state killing is reported; unknown.

state_response.shootings.summary: No event-specific firearm shooting is reported; unknown.

eligibility.summary: Contemporary reports establish a public gathering substantially over 50 and demands directed to Serbia’s government and institutions.

notes: The reported route and symbolic delivery establish the event’s program but not attendee departure; end remains unknown. Two outlets provide different attendance accounts, both over threshold; their source dependence is not established. A September follow-up describes a later protest and an organizer’s view that little had changed since January, not an explicit January response. A 19 February Eko straža open letter says the Prime Minister had not answered the submitted demands after 30 days; it reports public presidential remarks but says they did not address the demands. The ignore coding is based on this explicit first-party nonresponse claim, with exact submission date and official receipt still unverified.
open_questions: Did participants physically depart after demands were attached to the Government building?
Did authorities receive or formally respond to demands after the event?
Was the earlier June clean-air protest a separate gathering, and what year/date was it?
Were simultaneous protests actually held elsewhere on 10 January?

title: Internet freelancers protest retroactive taxation in Belgrade
location: Belgrade: National Assembly, march through central streets to the Government building and Slavija
scope: Belgrade gathering. Participants came from several Serbian cities; no simultaneous separate event outside Belgrade is established.
organizer: Association of Internet Workers (Udruženje radnika na internetu)
participants_original: Nova.rs reporter: “several thousand.” RFE/RL does not quantify the 16 January crowd; its “several hundred” figure is explicitly about the separate 30 December protest.
threshold_50_evidence: Nova.rs reports several thousand at the 16 January protest. RFE/RL does not provide a January attendance count, and its separate several-hundred estimate concerns 30 December.

title.summary: Contemporary sources describe the freelancers/internet workers protest against retroactive taxation.

start_date.summary: Both articles report the gathering on 16 January 2021.

end_date.summary: The Nova.rs article gives a route and an expected return but no departure/dissolution; RFE/RL reports the march reaching Slavija but no physical end. Unknown.

location.summary: Both report a gathering at the National Assembly followed by a march to the Government area and central Belgrade; Nova.rs also names the route back.

scope.summary: The gathering was in Belgrade; participants came from several cities, but no other contemporaneous site is established.

organizer.summary: The Association of Internet Workers is named as organizer.

demands.summary: The group demanded an end to retroactive tax collection and negotiations/new legislation governing internet workers. The codes capture tax policy and state policy affecting labor status.

participants_original.summary: Nova.rs says several thousand attended; RFE/RL does not quantify this event. Its several-hundred statement is for the Dec 30 protest and is not imported.

participants_min.summary: No exact numerical lower bound is assigned to the qualitative “several thousand” description.

participants_max.summary: No exact upper bound is reported.

protester_violence.summary: The reviewed articles do not report event-specific protester violence; unknown.

state_response.accommodation.summary: The PM’s office formally invited organizers at the 16 January protest to talks. Nova.rs reports that the 18 January meeting with the Prime Minister, finance minister and tax-administration director then took place; freelancers presented demands and negotiations were to continue. This qualifies as accommodation under the manual’s negotiation/formal-meeting rule. It does not establish that demands were accepted or settled. The 021/Nova pre-meeting article is schedule evidence, not an independent meeting outcome account.

state_response.arrests.summary: No arrest report appears in reviewed coverage; unknown.

state_response.beatings.summary: No beating report appears in reviewed coverage; unknown.

state_response.crowd_dispersal.summary: No crowd-dispersal mechanism is described; unknown.

state_response.ignore.summary: The government invited formal negotiations; no explicit refusal/avoidance is reported for this gathering. Other response remains unknown.

state_response.killings.summary: No event-specific state killing is reported; unknown.

state_response.shootings.summary: No event-specific firearm shooting is reported; unknown.

eligibility.summary: A large public gathering and state-directed tax/labor-policy demands are documented.

episode_boundary.summary: RFE/RL calls 16 January the second freelancer protest after the physically distinct 30 December gathering; its opened December report describes a short road blockage cleared at organizers’ request but no departure or continuous action through January. A February 21 Glas Šumadije article republished from Nova.rs describes later city assemblies without dating earlier gatherings. The shared campaign alone does not establish physical continuity.

notes: RFE/RL explicitly calls this the second protest after a distinct 30 December 2020 gathering. Its opened report on 30 December describes several hundred attendees and a brief traffic blockage that organizers asked participants to clear, but does not report departure/dissolution or action continuing to 16 January. The prior campaign onset therefore does not establish physical continuity; the 16 January assembly is retained as a separate candidate event unless continuous action is shown. The PM’s office invited the organizers to formal talks for 18 January; Nova.rs reports that the 18 January meeting took place and that negotiations would continue; this confirms accommodation but not acceptance of demands or the outcome of later talks. A Nova.rs search lead whose title suggested a new freelancer protest resolves to a page scheduling the 16 January gathering, not evidence of a 29 January event.
open_questions: What physical end is documented for 16 January?
Can another opened contemporaneous source independently corroborate January 16 attendance?
Was there a distinct physical freelancer gathering on 29 January? The reviewed Nova.rs page with that search-result title only refers to 16 January.
What outcome followed the 18 January meeting, and on which dates did later negotiations take place?
